boundary: This is the finite consumer-MVP Ganesha lane, not every Ganesha text, temple, form, festival, family practice, regional tradition, or historical claim.
completion_rule: Every accepted story family has a substantial beginning-to-end English and Hindi scene sequence; every accepted practice lane meets the ritual contract for its named applicability; every selected temple has a current evidence-scoped bilingual record; all required characters, places, and living connections are represented; and every remaining selected-scope gap is zero or explicitly blocked.

story_families.title_en: The four-yuga Ganesha Purana narrative spine
story_families.selected_expression: Exact pinned Sanskrit Wikisource Ganesha Purana, Krida Khanda 1-155
story_families.source_scope: Krida Khanda chapters 1-155, reconciled through the four principal avatar movements without claiming every discourse passage is a separate consumer scene
story_families.required_terminal: The selected expression's Krida Khanda and whole-work closing formulas

story_families.title_en: Parvati's guardian, the battle at the doorway, and Ganesha's restoration
story_families.title_hi: पार्वती का द्वारपाल, द्वार का संघर्ष और गणेश का पुनर्जीवन
story_families.selected_expression: Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita, Kumara Khanda 13-18
story_families.source_scope: One explicitly Shiva-Purana account; other birth accounts remain variants rather than corrections
story_families.required_terminal: Ganesha restored, recognized, and given his place among the ganas

story_families.title_en: The brothers' journey and Ganesha's circumambulation of his parents
story_families.title_hi: दो भाइयों की यात्रा और गणेश की माता-पिता की परिक्रमा
story_families.selected_expression: Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita, Kumara Khanda 19-20
story_families.source_scope: The selected Shiva-Purana family contest and its consequence; not a universal account of Kartikeya's family relations
story_families.required_terminal: The contest is resolved and its family consequences are retained

story_families.title_en: Vyasa and Ganesha make the Mahabharata writable
story_families.title_hi: व्यास और गणेश महाभारत को लिखित रूप देते हैं
story_families.selected_expression: K. M. Ganguli Mahabharata, Adi Parva section 1
story_families.source_scope: The selected Ganguli expression, while disclosing that the scribe episode is not present in the critical-edition main text
story_families.required_terminal: The conditions, composition, and writing collaboration are complete

story_families.title_en: Parashurama, the guarded doorway, and the broken tusk
story_families.title_hi: परशुराम, रोका गया द्वार और टूटा हुआ दाँत
story_families.selected_expression: Brahma Vaivarta Purana, Ganesa Khanda 42-45, Rajendra Nath Sen 1920 English expression
story_families.source_scope: One source-attributed explanation of Ekadanta; other broken-tusk accounts remain separately named variants
story_families.required_terminal: Conflict, injury, response, and reconciliation are complete

story_families.title_en: Ganesha and Tulasi: desire, refusal, and mutual curses
story_families.title_hi: गणेश और तुलसी: इच्छा, अस्वीकार और परस्पर शाप
story_families.selected_expression: Brahma Vaivarta Purana, Ganesa Khanda 46, Rajendra Nath Sen 1920 English expression
story_families.source_scope: A period-bound Puranic encounter; it is not modern relationship advice and does not erase Tulasi's later sacred standing
story_families.required_terminal: Both speeches, consequences, and the narrative's closing resolution are retained

blocked_story_extensions.reason: The retained nine-khanda carrier is internal_only_rights_review_pending, has no usable text layer or translation, and cannot lawfully ground consumer copy in this lane.
blocked_story_extensions.required_to_unblock: A product-cleared fixed expression plus source-aligned English/Hindi translation or independently reviewable transcription.

blocked_story_extensions.reason: The consumer MVP selects and labels representative fixed expressions; an exhaustive all-Purana variant concordance is a later denominator.

practice_lanes.applicability: West India Smarta household or individual, with family practice taking priority
A visitor or community participant in a Maharashtra public Ganeshotsav; not pandal management or priest-led liturgy
A Goa household participant seeking a scoped Chavath orientation; established family practice takes priority
A Tamil Nadu household participant seeking a bounded Pillaiyar/Vinayaka Chaturthi orientation; not a pan-South-India universal ritual

required_character_families: Parvati, Shiva, Kartikeya, and the Shiva ganas
Vyasa and Brahma in the selected Mahabharata scribe account
Parashurama in the selected broken-tusk account
Tulasi in the selected Brahma Vaivarta account
the four principal Ganesha Purana avatar movements and their named opponents/allies
Riddhi and Siddhi only where the selected expression or living temple evidence supports them
Mushika only with source-specific identity and role
required_place_families: the composition setting of the selected Mahabharata scribe account without invented coordinates
the places traversed by the selected Ganesha Purana narrative spine
Mumbai and Pune public Ganeshotsav contexts
living_connection_requirements: Each story family links to Ganesha and its source expression.
Ganesh Chaturthi links to the household, public-participant, Goa, and Tamil Nadu lanes without treating them as one procedure.
The Ashtavinayak circuit links eight distinct temple identities without collapsing their local narratives.
Temple sacred narratives, institutional history, current worship, and visitor facts remain separate claim scopes.
Cross-lane identities are submitted as typed proposals; unresolved owner-lane targets remain unresolved.
